newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Scania blames strong crown, markets.
newsitem.headline: Scania blames strong crown, markets.

text.p: Swedish bus and truck maker Scania said on Tuesday that a strong Swedish crown and uncertainty on European markets caused a 44 percent fall in 1996 profits.
Scania said the crown hit profits by 900 million crowns and uncertainty increased on its European markets in the fourth quarter of 1996.
Scania said changing over to the new 4-series had cost 650 million crowns.
"In 1996, we carried out the biggest production series change Scania has ever done," said Scania Managing Director Leif Ostling.

Ostling added that uncertainty in Europe had affected results and order intake there had fallen by 15 percent. "The uncertainty even increased in January 1997 when order intake was 5.0 percent lower than in January 1996," he said.

"Despite increased competition, we increased our market share in western Europe with around one percentage point to 15.5 percent. We now stand well equipped for the future with a new generation of trucks, busses and engines," he added.
Scania said its market share in Brazil rose in 1996 to 38.2 percent from 33.9 percent.
